briefdescription.para: Decorator presenting a small-strain (hypoelastic) material as a finite-strain material.

detaileddescription.para:
BaseMaterialType
A concrete class derived from MarmotMaterialHypoElastic.
tangentMode
How the algorithmic tangent is evaluated, see Marmot::Materials::HughesWingetTangent.
The wrapped material is driven by the objective strain increment of the Hughes-Winget algorithm, evaluated on the mid-step configuration, \[ \Delta\boldsymbol{l} = \left(\boldsymbol{F}^{(n+1)} - \boldsymbol{F}^{(n)}\right) \boldsymbol{F}_{\text{mid}}^{-1}, \qquad \boldsymbol{F}_{\text{mid}} = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\boldsymbol{F}^{(n)} + \boldsymbol{F}^{(n+1)}\right), \] split into its symmetric and skew parts $ \Delta\boldsymbol{\varepsilon} $ and $ \Delta\boldsymbol{\Omega} $. The incremental rotation follows from the Cayley transform \[ \Delta\boldsymbol{R} = \left(\boldsymbol{I} - \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta\boldsymbol{\Omega}\right)^{-1} \left(\boldsymbol{I} + \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta\boldsymbol{\Omega}\right), \] which is orthogonal to machine precision. The stress carried over from the previous increment is rotated forward, $ \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\text{rot}} = \Delta\boldsymbol{R}\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{(n)} \Delta\boldsymbol{R}^{T} $, the wrapped material is evaluated, and the resulting Cauchy stress is pushed to the Kirchhoff stress $ \boldsymbol{\tau} = J\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{(n+1)} $ expected by the finite-strain consumers.

simplesect.para: Only the stress is rotated. Tensor-valued internal variables of the wrapped material (kinematic hardening back stresses, plastic strain tensors, anisotropic damage tensors) are passed through untouched and are therefore not objective under large incremental rotations. Models whose internal state is scalar or isotropic-invariant are unaffected.

The characteristic element length is not derived from any geometry here. It must be assigned explicitly via setCharacteristicElementLength; until then it is NaN, so a wrapped material that relies on it fails loudly instead of silently regularising incorrectly.
